claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do have a child - my son Alex, he's 7 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. It's good to know that Alex is 7 years old and lives with you.

Now, do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. Since you're living abroad, there are specific circumstances where you may still be eligible for Child Benefit.

Can you tell me which country you're currently living in, and whether you or your partner work as a Crown servant (such as a diplomat or member of HM Forces stationed abroad)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm currently living in Spain. No, neither my partner nor I work as Crown servants - we don't work for the diplomatic service or HM Forces or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since you're living in Spain and not working as a Crown servant, I need to understand a bit more about your situation.

Are you an EU, EEA, or Swiss national, or do you have any status under the EU Settlement Scheme (such as settled or pre-settled status)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't have any of those statuses. I'm just a British citizen living in Spain, but I don't have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. 

Just to confirm - are you planning to return to the UK, or are you permanently residing in Spain? And when did you move to Spain?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I moved to Spain about a year ago, and I'm living here permanently now. I don't have any plans to return to the UK at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: While Alex is 7 years old and lives with you (which would normally meet the basic requirements), the main issue is the residency requirement. To qualify for Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK. 

There are exceptions for people living abroad, such as if you're a Crown servant (diplomat, HM Forces member, etc.) or living in certain specific countries under particular circumstances. However, since you're living permanently in Spain and are not working as a Crown servant, you don't meet the exceptions that would allow you to claim Child Benefit while living abroad.

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. If your circumstances change in the future - for example, if you return to live in the UK - you would be able to claim Child Benefit at that time.
